scope: Current presentation portraits, rendered from archived counts or numerical states. Original figures and numerical packets are not overwritten.

rows.title: Icosahedral Gaussian flow
rows.description: Cases 177 and 183 are three-state autonomous flows. Long integrations and independent solvers support chaotic motion; absorbing balls and local equilibria are interval certified. The directed geometric skeleton has a known integrable counterpart.
rows.coordinates: Full three-state coordinates; archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: Tetrahedral Gaussian flow
rows.description: Cases 421 and 565 have a stable central equilibrium and sustained irregular outer motion. Three-dimensional tetrahedral chaos is established prior work.
rows.coordinates: Full three-state coordinates; archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: Localized Gaussian vortices
rows.description: Case 77 survives a 30,000-unit spectrum and independent integration. A competing periodic orbit and resemblance to known threefold geometries limit interpretation.
rows.coordinates: Full three-state coordinates; archived orthographic camera.

rows.title: Dissipative three-axis twist map
rows.description: Cases 1709 and 3254 retain positive finite-time growth under long and high-precision controls. The first case also has a regular regime.
rows.coordinates: Full three-state coordinates; archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: RAAR between spatial circles
rows.description: Case 1051 has a certified attracting positive-entropy set containing the symbolic dynamics and a Whitney fold. Transitivity and equality with the numerical portrait remain unresolved. Case 1483 is a numerical companion.
rows.coordinates: Full spatial state (x, y, z); archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: RAAR with finite spatial point sets
rows.description: Numerical candidates in a known projection algorithm. Five-million-step observations and 33-start cohorts retain positive finite-time growth. Finite-alphabet phase retrieval is established prior art; historical uniqueness remains open.
rows.coordinates: Full three-state iterates, centered and rigidly rotated. Equal spatial units within each panel; independent scales. Two million consecutive states per static portrait.

rows.title: Gaussian posterior mean and a circle
rows.description: Case 156 has a certified connected attracting set with entropy at least log(2)/6 and mixed-index periodic points. Opposite orientation signs force failure of local injectivity on the set, excluding ambient neighborhood conjugacy to locally injective maps. Intrinsic equivalence and historical novelty remain unresolved. Case 29 remains numerical.
rows.coordinates: Full three-state iterates; centering, orthogonal principal-axis basis, and rigid orthographic camera. Equal spatial units within each panel; independent scales.

rows.title: Gaussian posterior mean and a sphere
rows.description: Cases 155 and 251 retain positive finite-time growth over five million steps, 33 starts and independent 70/100-digit checks. Folded spatial candidates in a known reflection construction; asymptotic attraction and historical uniqueness remain unresolved.
rows.coordinates: Native three-state iterates, centered and orthogonally rotated; equal units within each panel. Independent spatial scales and density saturation.

rows.title: Canonical posterior maps: ribbon and spatial folds
rows.description: Cases 163 and 653 have simple canonical site parameters and retain positive finite-time growth across long runs, fresh starts and high precision. Case 653 has two positive mean QR rates. Asymptotic chaotic attraction and historical uniqueness remain unresolved.
rows.coordinates: Native three-state iterates; orthogonal cameras and equal spatial units within each panel.

rows.title: Product-alphabet posterior maps
rows.description: Case 988 forms a four-wing spatial cloud and retains positive finite-time growth across 33 starts and precision controls. Case 489 forms layered arches with competing fixed outcomes. Known posterior/reflection ingredients, periodic parameter windows and unresolved historical uniqueness are documented.
rows.coordinates: Native three-state iterates; rigid orthogonal camera and equal spatial units within each panel. Independent panel scales and density saturation.

rows.title: Nonuniform product posteriors
rows.description: Folded-shell numerical Cases 6 and 7: positive finite growth at 33 starts and 70/100 digits. Toroidal motifs are known; attraction, topology and historical uniqueness remain open.
rows.coordinates: Native discrete three-state iterates; orthogonal cameras and equal units within panels. Independent panel scales and density saturation.

rows.title: Finite-point RAAR: fragmented columns and sheets

rows.coordinates: Full three-state iterates, centered and rigidly rotated. Equal spatial units within each panel; independent scales. Two million consecutive states per static portrait.

rows.title: Finite-point RAAR: fans and sparse branches
rows.description: Numerical candidates in a known projection algorithm. Five-million-step observations and 33-start cohorts retain positive finite-time growth. Finite-alphabet phase retrieval is established prior art; historical uniqueness remains open.

rows.title: Scalar iteration with acceleration memory
rows.description: Plain scalar iteration is globally convergent for the two selected maps. Regularized three-history acceleration instead produces persistent irregular memory states, checked at 80 and 110 digits.
rows.coordinates: Three-history state; archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: RK45 step-size controller
rows.description: The physical linear oscillator decays. The adaptive solver has a persistent irregular internal state near its error tolerance, reproduced with the original library and high-precision arithmetic.
rows.coordinates: Position / atol, velocity / atol, proposed step; archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: RK23 step-size controller
rows.description: The physical linear oscillator decays. The adaptive solver has a persistent irregular internal state near its error tolerance, reproduced with the original library and high-precision arithmetic.

rows.title: Smooth Yogi memory
rows.description: The published tanh variant produces two positive finite growth rates in selected scalar-quadratic regimes. Independent high-precision and TensorFlow controls support the calculations.
rows.coordinates: Normalized optimizer state (x, m, v); archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: Matrix scaling with unequal rates
rows.description: Cases 150 and 987 retain two positive finite QR rates after 106 million steps and pass 70/100-digit controls. Trapping, asymptotic chaotic attraction and historical uniqueness remain unresolved.
rows.coordinates: All three anchored log coordinates; translation and proper orthogonal PCA rotation, with equal units and no rescaling. Each panel contains 250000 consecutive final states.

rows.title: Yogi parameter-plane candidate
rows.description: Case 670 is retained after five million steps and independent controls. Case 125 has stronger evidence for a second expanding direction; their rates remain finite-time quantities.
rows.coordinates: Normalized optimizer state (x, m, v); archived orthographic camera.

rows.title: Yogi memory
rows.description: Cases 44 and 7590 are visually distinct numerical regimes of the same published optimizer. Initialization and precision controls are retained in the report.
rows.coordinates: Normalized optimizer state (x, m, v); archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: Yogi: additional expanding regimes
rows.description: Cases 4214 and 125 have numerical evidence for two expanding directions. Window lengths, library differences and branch discontinuities are reported separately.
rows.coordinates: Normalized optimizer states; archived preview cameras. Panels have separate scales.

rows.title: Adamax memory
rows.description: Four-million-step, high-precision and PyTorch controls support the selected regimes. Case 4099 coexists with two reflected periodic orbits.
rows.coordinates: Normalized optimizer state; archived orthographic cameras.

rows.title: AdaBelief memory
rows.description: A scalar quadratic objective supports irregular full optimizer states at the selected memory parameters. Finite-time numerical evidence is separated from convergence and novelty claims.
rows.coordinates: Normalized state (x, m, s); equal displayed coordinate units.

rows.title: Four motor rows
rows.description: At fixed mechanical parameters, b=1.5 gives a narrow braid and b=1.545 a broader regime. Long full-spectrum integrations support chaos in both; the displayed geometry is a projection of an eleven-dimensional flow.
rows.coordinates: Three orthonormal displacement contrasts; final 1,200 saved time units; common scale.

rows.title: Five motor rows
rows.description: The same saved fourteen-dimensional trajectory is shown in two projections of its four displacement contrasts. Neither view defines a three-dimensional embedding.
rows.coordinates: Fourier displacement contrasts; final 800 saved time units.

rows.title: Three motor rows with unequal rates
rows.description: Case 2566 is an eight-dimensional numerical candidate. The projection uses a fixed orthogonal rotation of the three cosine occupancies.
rows.coordinates: Rotated cosine occupancies; final 600 saved time units; stride 2.

rows.title: Eight motor rows: periodic and irregular motion
rows.description: A five-cluster periodic attractor is certified in all 23 state dimensions. The irregular comparison has six positive finite-time exponents over 20,000 units; it is not a certified chaotic attractor.
rows.coordinates: Physical coordinates (X0, X1, s0) of the 23D model; common scale.

rows.title: Three symmetric motor rows
rows.description: Case 783 has an independently computed eight-dimensional spectrum with one positive and one near-zero rate. This image shows the three sine occupancies.
rows.coordinates: Sine occupancies (s0, s1, s2); a projection of the 8D flow.

rows.title: Motor-pair model
rows.description: Case 444 retains positive growth in a long independent CPU calculation. The neutral rate still needs convergence; priority and asymptotic attraction remain unresolved.
rows.coordinates: Physical coordinates (h, Y, Z); final 2,000 saved time units.

rows.title: Synchronematic oscillators
rows.description: The four-particle candidate is displayed through gauge-invariant collective observables. These do not form an embedding of the seven-dimensional reduced angular dynamics.
rows.coordinates: Collective observables (Re Q, Im Q, C), not state coordinates.

rows.title: Light-driven elastomer slider
rows.description: The retained regime belongs to a three-state relay model. The report separates transverse growth estimates, switching assumptions and known related mechanisms.
rows.coordinates: Scaled full state (u/q, v/(sqrt(k) q), phi/q); scaling is explicitly physical.

rows.title: Two-strain epidemic model
rows.description: The numerical five-state regime contains unequal outbreaks and extremely small prevalence. Related epidemic chaos is established; physical interpretation requires the qualifications in the report.
rows.coordinates: Projection (S, 1000 I1, 1000 I2); explicit axis units, not an embedding.

rows.title: Coupled optical operators
rows.description: These six-state relay histories have persistent irregular motion in the recorded observation. Later continuations, captures and source-model assumptions are retained in the report.
rows.coordinates: Projection (x_minus, x_plus, y_minus - y_plus); all saved adaptive event/QR knots.
rows.sampling_note: The knots are nonuniform in time. Point density is sampling density, not an invariant measure.

rows.title: Smooth optical feedback
rows.description: At the same logistic-width parameters, saved starts produce regular and irregular histories. This is a finite coexistence observation, not an asymptotic attractor classification.
rows.coordinates: Projection (x_minus, x_plus, y_minus - y_plus); common scale.

rows.title: Finite-sample FastICA
rows.description: Cases 204 and 351 retain positive finite-time tangent growth over five million steps and at 70 and 100 digits. Case 351 has regular competing outcomes. These are regimes of an established algorithm; historical priority and asymptotic chaotic attraction remain unresolved.
rows.coordinates: Projection of the unit weight on (w1, w2, w4); every consecutive state is retained. No sign folding. Spatial scale and density saturation differ between panels.

rows.title: Structured-data FastICA
rows.description: An explicit finite-data construction has a certified attracting positive-entropy set for 0 <= epsilon <= 1/25. The epsilon=0.15 companion is numerical only. Expanding-circle dynamics are known; historical priority of this realization is unresolved.
rows.coordinates: Projection (A,B,C) of a unit weight in S3; D is omitted. Equal units, common scale, 500000 consecutive states per panel; no sign folding.
